clue.text: One suffers a lot of unhappiness, according to Gilbert

definitions.text: One suffers a lot of unhappiness, according to Gilbert

parts.words: One suffers a lot of unhappiness, according to Gilbert
parts.note: points to the Gilbert and Sullivan song in The Pirates of Penzance whose refrain says a certain officer's lot is not a happy one

explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for the comic operas of Gilbert and Sullivan; the sergeant's song in The Pirates of Penzance laments that his 'lot' is not a happy one.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer of that Gilbert lament is a police sergeant, so the sufferer is a member of the constabulary.

clue.text: Sort of book that has outstanding illustrations

definitions.text: Sort of book that has outstanding illustrations

parts.words: Sort of book that has outstanding illustrations
parts.note: outstanding is read literally: the pictures stand out from the page when it is opened

explanation.definitionFit: Children's books with folded cardboard pictures that rise up as the pages open are named for that springing motion.

clue.text: Composing music for children

parts.note: composing is read as calming or settling, not writing music: a soothing song sung to send a child to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Composing' pretends to mean writing music; here it means making calm, as in composing oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle song is gentle music sung to calm a little one into sleep.

clue.text: Dreadful cover on the French record

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second, covering it from above

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad or dreadful
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone complains about an awful lid on a French dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' here is the informal British sense of awful, not the medical sense of long-lasting; 'cover on' works because in a down answer the first piece sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical account set down in order of events is a written record.

clue.text: Assemble a lot of people in crowd for dictator

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people
pro means in favour of, for
Il Duce was the title of the Italian dictator Mussolini

explanation.surface: A tyrant gathers many people into a crowd for a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture goods in great quantity on a production line is to build large numbers of them.

clue.text: Game found in animal sanctuary

indicators.note: found in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Wildlife is discovered living in a reserve for creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is concealed in 'aNIMal'; 'sanctuary' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Nim is a mathematical strategy game in which players take turns removing objects from heaps.

clue.text: Italian singer has fish, followed by duck

indicators.note: followed by places the next piece after the one before it

parts.note: the bass is a fish
in cricket a duck is a score of nought, written as O

explanation.surface: An Italian vocalist owns a fish and then a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is cricket's word for a batter's score of zero, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Basso is the Italian term for a bass singer, the lowest male voice.

clue.text: Something purchased to protect soldier's head, note

definitions.text: Something purchased to protect soldier's head, note

indicators.note: the bought item wraps around the other letters as if guarding them

parts.note: a buy is something bought

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word soldier's

parts.note: B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A purchase guards a soldier's head, someone notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the tall fur hat worn by some British soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A busby is a tall fur cap worn on parade by hussars and some guards regiments.

clue.text: Main wine of Bordeaux, for example

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: The chief wine of the Bordeaux region is discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is a French harbour city on the Garonne, a town where ships dock.

clue.text: Cricketing error produces defeat

definitions.meaning: in cricket a throw from a fielder that goes past the stumps and lets the batters run again
to topple or bring down a ruler or government

explanation.surface: A fielding blunder loses the match.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a wild return gifting extra runs carries that name; to topple a regime is also to defeat it.

clue.text: Nothing left in capital for star

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the city

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: With nothing remaining in the capital, someone goes off seeking fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the Pole Star, the bright star nearly above the north pole.

clue.text: Error bringing risk on motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written MI in crosswords
a stake is money put at risk in a bet

explanation.surface: A blunder causes danger on a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or blunder is a wrong act or judgement.

clue.text: Seafood still to be cooked put in empty pan

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside the other
empty means take out the middle of the word pan, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: raw food has not yet been cooked

explanation.surface: Uncooked seafood goes into a bare frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Act timidly as a cat's-paw?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a puss's foot; the question mark flags the jokey sense

explanation.surface: Someone timid is used as a dupe.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-paw usually means a person used as a tool by another; here it is just the animal's paw.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread warily and evasively is to avoid committing; a moggy's foot is literally the same pair of words.

clue.text: Honourable behaviour in orderly club

parts.note: straight means tidy or in order
a bat is a club for hitting a ball

explanation.surface: A well-run club behaves with honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Playing with a straight bat is a cricket image for decent, upright conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket phrase stands for honest, proper conduct by allusion to correct batting.

clue.text: Shy characters of 18?. Nothing odd in that

indicators.note: keeping none of the odd-placed letters of the 18-down answer leaves only the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: points to the answer at 18 down, ACRONYM

explanation.surface: Characters from another clue are modest; nothing peculiar there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters of 18' refers to the letters of the 18-down answer; drop the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy means bashful or reluctant to be forthcoming.

clue.text: Vessel going round a river boat

indicators.note: the container's letters go round the others

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
the Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall in England

explanation.surface: A ship circles a river craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is an English river forming most of the border between Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing craft.

clue.text: Rich maestro upset musical director

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A wealthy conductor upsets the music director.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who trains and conducts a group of singers in church directs its music.

clue.text: Fair game for uncle, presumably

parts.note: a fairground game in which balls are thrown at a figure, whose name sounds like an uncle's female relative

explanation.walkthrough: The fairground game of throwing at a dummy also gives a phrase for an easy target of criticism; an uncle's wife is an aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure in this old fairground throwing game is a target, an object of easy attack, and an uncle's spouse would be an aunt.

clue.text: Sun editor — an odd source of support for Labour

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper boss oddly backs the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid that has often opposed the Labour Party, hence 'odd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Organised labour bodies have long funded and backed the British Labour Party.

clue.text: An initial combination, it may be said

definitions.text: An initial combination, it may be said

parts.words: An initial combination, it may be said
parts.note: a word built from first letters of other words, and pronounced as a word

explanation.definitionFit: A term formed from initials and spoken as a single word, like NATO, fits that description.

clue.text: Seat often overlooked by minister

parts.note: overlooked means looked down on from the pulpit, not ignored: a church bench

explanation.definitionFit: A long bench in a church faces the pulpit, where the clergyman looks down on it.

clue.text: American serving in South American country and a European city

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the following letters

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America
GI is a US soldier, an American serving in the forces

explanation.surface: A US soldier is stationed in Peru and later in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Perugia is the capital of Umbria in central Italy.

clue.text: Month in which libertine enters African city

indicators.note: enters means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: March is a month
a rake is a dissolute man, a libertine

explanation.surface: A playboy arrives in an African city in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrakech is a major city of Morocco in North Africa.

clue.text: Escape from a heartless situation, perhaps

parts.note: an empty space with nothing at its heart is a void

explanation.surface: Someone flees an unfeeling situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' suggests cruelty, but here it means hollow at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer clear of something is to evade or escape it.

clue.text: Is inspiring in retreat, showing a little bit of character

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: fires means inspires or stirs up

explanation.surface: Someone shows character by inspiring others while retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reverses FIRES; 'character' is a printed letter, not a person's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a printed letter, part of a typographic character.

clue.text: Ostentatious mark on uniform

definitions.meaning: showy and gaudy, especially in display of wealth
a coloured patch or badge on a military uniform

explanation.surface: A showy badge decorates a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy display is called that in British slang, and a cloth insignia on a soldier's sleeve bears the same name.

clue.text: Criticise summary

definitions.meaning: a brief account of the main points

explanation.surface: Someone attacks an abstract.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone is to talk them down; a quick outline of points is also given that name.

clue.text: Son initially leaves one card game for another

indicators.note: the son's abbreviation leaves from the front of the word

parts.note: snap is a card game

explanation.surface: A son leaves one card game for another.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for son; nap, short for Napoleon, is an old card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap is a trick-taking card game, so it is a different card game from snap.

clue.text: City's third in table on goal difference

indicators.note: third in means the third letter of the word table
difference suggests the letters are made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: A city ranks third in the league table on goal difference.
explanation.walkthrough: Football tables separate level teams on goal difference; here it shuffles ON GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a historic city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Unsettled type a loyal friend backed

indicators.note: backed means turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: Damon of classical legend was the faithful friend of Pythias

explanation.surface: A wanderer is supported by a faithful friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon and Pythias are the Greek pair famous for loyal friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is restless, never settled in one place.

clue.text: Change needed in office

parts.note: change means small coins, not alteration: the small fund kept for minor workplace expenses

explanation.definitionFit: A small float of money held in a workplace pays for minor purchases.
